text:
luca: Heads-up: I saw a flaky docs build in the release branch due to an mdx shortcode that includes a code sample with backticks. The html sanitizer strips the fence and CI fails the examples test.
nina: Which page?
luca: docs/guides/embedding-best-practices.mdx — snippet: 
```mdx
```bash
# upload embeddings
redwood upload --file data.csv --model embed-1
```
```
The sanitizer converted triple backticks into single backticks in the rendered HTML.
ci-bot: Build #4523 failed: code fence sanitization mismatch.
pat: That sounds like the mdx parser version drift between local and CI (we bumped remark/rehype in a dependency earlier). Could be the rehype-sanitize policy.
nina: Quick fix: escape the fence in the source by wrapping the snippet in an HTML comment hack or use indented code blocks. But better: pin the remark plugins and ensure the same rehype-sanitize schema in CI and local.
luca: I opened PR 1245 that pins remark-mdx and the rehype plugins in package.json and adds a small test: render the examples page and assert code fences are preserved.
pat: Nice. Add a tiny fixture that includes ```` ```bash ... ``` ```` to catch regressions.
ci-bot: PR 1245 lint checks passed locally.
nina: LGTM, will merge after CI.
